entries.0:
Product guide

Scroll inside this editor and watch the active item in the outline below. This document starts at H2 on purpose, so an H1 is not required.

The content is long enough to show how the outline follows a real article, help center page, or internal document.

Plan the document

Start with the questions your reader needs answered. Group related details into sections that are easy to scan.

Use headings for structure rather than appearance. A clear outline helps readers understand where they are and what comes next.

Keep the most important sections near the top, then move supporting detail into smaller subsections.

Name sections clearly

Prefer short labels that describe the outcome, such as Configure the editor or Publish the article.

The same labels appear in the table of contents, so they should still make sense without the paragraphs around them.

Configure the editor

Add the Tiptap editor to a Group with a fixed height. Turn on overflow scrolling for that Group when the document should stay inside a compact panel.

The editor can also grow with the page. Choose the layout that matches the reading experience in your app.

Initial content can come from plain text, HTML, Tiptap JSON, or a field on a Bubble Thing.

Enable the outline

Turn on the Table of contents extension and Unique ID. The editor then publishes its Table of contents (JSON) state.

Headings can begin at H2, H3, or another level. The visual outline normalizes them into a readable hierarchy.

Bind the live outline

Add the Tiptap Table of Contents visual element outside the editor’s scroll frame.

Set its Table of contents JSON field to this editor’s Table of contents (JSON) state. No custom JavaScript is required.

As the reader scrolls, the active and scrolled-over states update automatically.

Style active sections

Choose normal, scrolled-over, and active colors. You can also control indentation, item spacing, font weight, and the active indicator.

Use enough contrast to make the current section clear without distracting from the document.

Replace content safely

You can load another Thing through Initial content, auto-binding, or the Set Content action.

The editor republishes the outline when the document changes, and the visual element replaces stale headings.

This makes the same editor and outline reusable across articles, records, and URL-driven pages.

Test the experience

Scroll from the first section to the last. Check that the active item follows the document and that clicking an outline item reaches the correct heading.

Also test documents with no H1, skipped heading levels, and content that changes without a full page reload.

On mobile, keep tap targets comfortable and confirm that the editor does not introduce horizontal overflow.

Ship an accessible navigation

Give the outline a useful accessible label such as On this page. The visual element renders semantic navigation and links.

Readers can now scan, scroll, and jump through a long document without losing their place.
Start writing. Type # then space for a heading.

1. Turn on Table of contents in the Tiptap element.
2. Add the Tiptap Table of Contents visual element.
3. Set its Table of contents JSON field to the editor’s Table of contents (JSON) state.

The outline refreshes when headings are edited or the editor loads different content. Documents can start at H2–H6; they do not need an H1.
How you would wire this in your app.
Scroll inside the editor and watch the active item move through the separate Table of Contents element. Edit any heading and the outline updates from the editor’s Bubble state.
A table of contents that follows your document.

1. Draw two groups. Set unique ID to e.g. notionBubbleMenu and notionFloatingMenu.
2. Put buttons in those groups. Wire them to Tiptap actions.
3. On Tiptap, set Bubble menu / Floating menu to those IDs.
4. Turn on Drag Handle.

Copy this reusable. Keep the unique IDs unique if you put two editors on one page.
Bubble menu on selection, floating menu on empty lines, drag handle on blocks. The menus are Bubble groups. Tiptap only needs their unique IDs.

properties.text: Let the page grow, or scroll inside the editor.
Fit height on = the editor grows and the page scrolls. Wrap Tiptap in a fixed-height group with overflow scroll = only the editor scrolls.

Grow: Tiptap fit height = yes.
Scroll inside: put Tiptap in a group with a fixed height and overflow scroll. Leave Tiptap fit height on so the document can be taller than the box.
